Seidenfaden in his study of a similar orchid from Thailand, prefered to keep his plant under G. siamensis Rolfe ex Downie, with the remark that he dare not s p i l the type specimen by dissecting and that until fresh material is available from Khasi hills (underlining ours) we will have to rely on Hook. f.'s figure (Ic. Apart from the type, Seidenfaden had seen a specimen of Prain at Kew. Hooker him- self had remarked that he "had great difi- cul~y in analpsing the flowers of this singu- lir species". At the Calcutta Herbarium there is a suit of g specimens (each sheer with 2 - 6 plants) of Dr. Prain's collector - (dung Lepcho) 26 from Shillong gathered in 1899. Two of these bear indications of having been referred by Dr. Prain to Rolfe at Kew, who had compared with Hooker's specimen and Icones. The single Prain specimen at Kew is evidently one of this batch. After the long intervals of 1850 and 1899, ihis is the first collection of this rare orchid. Incidentally, this is almost a paral- lel to a similar rare collection of a closely related saprophytic crchid Didymoplexis (Rao et al. in Bull. Surv. A study of the available old material, dis- section of freshly collected flowers in com- parison with the illustrations, including that of Seidenfaderl has led us to conclude that G. siamensis is only G. exilis, and to 4 I 6. 1925 syn. ; Seidenf. in Bot. Tids- skrift 65: 106.

Roots sparse, long, slender, branched. lnJ?orescence a terminal raceme, 3 - 20 cm long, 3 - 25-Rowered, lax, sub- secund, long scaped. Floral bracts ca 4 . 0 ~ 1.5 mm, ovate-lanceo- late, obtuse to acute, shorter than the ovary plus pedicel,- brown. Flowers ca 1.5 cm long, tubular, milky white ; perianth sparse- ly gland dotted. Ovary with pedicel ca g mnl long, slightly curved. Sepals con- nate into a ventricose tube with 3 lobes at the mouth ; tube ca 10 x 5 mm ; lobes ca 2 x2.o-2.5 Inm, triangular or ovate, longer than the petals, irregularly laciniate and crisped at margins (laciniations more and shorter than those of petals), 3-nerved. Petals ca I .5 x I .o mm, inserted on the tube alternating the sepaline lobes, subrhomboid- a1 or obovate, obtuse, irregularly laciniate and crisped at margins, I-nerved. INDIA VOL. 22 (I-4), I 980 20.5 globose or reniform outgrowths (calli) to- wards the base on the claw. Column ca 4.5 mm long, winged at the margins, with two erect short acute teeth ; anther terrn- inal, hinged to the column, 2-celled ; polli- nia granular, in two groups, yellow ; stigma towards the base of the column, its surface lobed. Capsules ca 4.0 x 0 8 cm, sub-secund, long stalked, 3 - 20, obovoid-ellipsoid, promi- nently s-ribed, with ~ersistent bracts, grey coloured, dehiscing by six vertical sutures ; seeds ca I rnm long, slender, fusiform ; testa cells rectangular, in vertical rows and with spirally thickened walls. Flowering and Fruiting: Oct. - NOV. MEGHALAYA : Jaintia Hills, Raliang (ca 500 rn), 27.10.19!30. Rae 73600, 77234 -flowering and A. Rao 77235-fruiting (ASSAM). In the lip being free from the tube of perianth and erose at margins, G. exilis dif- fers from G. orobanchoides Benth., the lip sf which adnater to the tube of perianth at base and entire at margins.

However, G. exilis is closer to G. dyerinna K. re- p9rted from Sikkim but differs in the flow- ers being suberect instead of pendulous ; in the sepaline lobes and petals being laciniate instead of entire. Brit. 1893 & Ill. Cyper. 1909 ; Saldanha & Nicolson, F1. Hassan 683. (CYPERACEAE) Clarke described this species from its type locality Secunderabad in Andhra Pradesh. Recently, Saldanha & Nicolson reported it from Hhssan District, Karnataka. In a scrutiny of specimens in the folders of F. cdi- aris (L.) Roxb. in MH, a few specimens were found to be of F. trilobites C. Clarke. One of the two specimens collected by Cherian Jacob from Salem District under ox8007 turned out to b; this species. It may be the c1ose exteinal ~irnilarit~ which had made him give the same number to the two specimens. The constant reliable character to distinguish the two species is the tip of the hypogynous scales. In F. trilobites ir is anchor shaped whereas in the other spe- cies it is clearly quadrate. The present ob- servation suggests a strong possibility of its wider distribution than what is known now. Specimen examined : TAMIL NADU : Salem Dt., Hoganakal, Cherian Jacob 018007 A (MH). Gamble established this species based on the collection of Bourdillon from Travan- core in 1857.
